why: the executor's node TABLE -- `nodes`, `node`, `node_mut`, `node_id_by_name`, `node_session_mut`, `node_builder`. static entity storage: the executor's entity table is an arena sized at compile time (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_HANDLES`) with no allocator behind it, and a `HandleId` is an index into it. Registration is one-way -- no slot is ever reclaimed and no handle is ever invalidated. A node is a record in a fixed table addressed by `NodeId`, not an `Arc<Node>` a caller keeps, so reaching one means asking the executor. RFC-0043/0044: the Rust API is a declarative component model.
